items.title: The Inedible Menu
items.question: Korzybski's dictum: the map is not the territory — a menu describes but never nourishes. Diners confusing glowing reviews with good meals commit what error?
items.correctExplanation: Mistaking representation for reality — reviews map meals; maps never nourish. Every confusion of sign for thing repeats the diner's error.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is mistaking representation for reality. Skepticism, budgets, and speed miss it: glowing text is a map, dinner the territory. Menus describe; only kitchens deliver.
items.lessonContent:
Menus describe; kitchens alone deliver.
Signs never nourish, however glowing.
Representation differs from reality structurally.
Confusing them is the primal error.
Share this: eat one meal unreviewed.

items.title: The Solid Abstraction
items.question: 'The economy demands sacrifice' — as if Economy were a beast with appetites. Treating abstract nouns as concrete agents has a name. What is it?
items.correctExplanation: Reification — thingifying abstractions: economies demand, markets punish, societies decide. Agents invented by grammar rule sentences.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is reification. Verification tests, falsification refutes, quantification counts — none make nouns into beasts. Abstractions govern sentences only when mistaken for agents.
items.lessonContent:
Nouns need not name agents to rule sentences.
Abstractions govern only when mistaken.
Beasts invented by grammar demand sacrifices.
De-agentify nouns before obeying them.
Share this: unmake one noun-beast today.

items.title: The Growing Number
items.question: GDP climbs while life satisfaction flatlines, rivers sicken, and leisure shrinks. As a map of national wellbeing, what does GDP omit?
choices: Everything that matters beyond market transactions
items.correctAnswer: Everything that matters beyond market transactions
items.correctExplanation: Everything beyond market transactions — unpaid care, nature, leisure, distribution: GDP maps spending, never living. Growth numbers can rise as lives thin.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is everything that matters beyond market transactions. Inflation, reserves, and arms miss it: the map excludes whole territories by design. Spending is counted; living is not.
items.lessonContent:
Spending counted differs from living measured.
Maps exclude territories by design choices.
Growth numbers can rise as lives thin.
Wellbeing needs wider cartography.
Share this: price one uncounted good.

items.title: The Single Number
items.question: An IQ score predicts school outcomes yet collapses memory, creativity, wisdom, and character into one integer. What does the number hide?
items.correctExplanation: Multidimensionality — one integer compresses many faculties: collapse loses the shape. Scores rank; they never describe.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is the multidimensionality of minds. Shoes, prices, and handwriting miss it: compression discards structure. Rankings predict crudely while misdescribing finely.
items.lessonContent:
Compression discards structure always.
Integers rank; they never describe.
Faculties pluralize beyond single scores.
Predictive crudity differs from faithful portrait.
Share this: describe one mind multidimensionally.

items.title: The Trust Score
items.question: Lenders reduce a life to three digits; landlords and employers follow. What does a credit score actually measure?
items.correctExplanation: Repayment history, narrowly — past debts serviced, nothing about worth, character, or fate. Three digits map one trail, not the traveler.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is repayment history, narrowly. Worth, character, and destiny miss it: the file records transactions, never souls. Trails mapped; travelers mistaken.
items.lessonContent:
Files record transactions, never souls.
Trails mapped differ from travelers judged.
Three digits narrow a life to debts.
Worth exceeds every scoring system.
Share this: separate one score from one soul.

items.title: The Graded Ghost
items.question: Straight-A transcripts can accompany hollow understanding when schooling optimizes marks over mastery. What have grades become?
choices: A map mistaken for the territory
items.correctAnswer: A map mistaken for the territory
items.correctExplanation: A map mistaken for territory — marks signal learning the way smoke signals fire, until schooling manufactures smokeless marks. Optimized signals decouple.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is a map mistaken for the territory. Perfection, randomness, and bribery miss it: grades map mastery until systems optimize the map itself. Hollow transcripts are Goodhart graduates.
items.lessonContent:
Optimized signals decouple from sources.
Smoke manufactured without fire fools all.
Mastery differs from its markers.
Systems teach to maps, not territories.
Share this: learn one thing ungraded.

items.title: The Useful Lie
items.question: Statistician Box wrote that all models are wrong but some are useful. What distinguishes a useful model from a worshipped one?
choices: Held lightly as a tool, not a truth
items.correctAnswer: Held lightly as a tool, not a truth
items.correctExplanation: Held lightly as tool — usefulness lives in provisional grip: predictions checked, limits known. Worshipped models graduate from instruments to idols.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is held lightly as a tool, not a truth. Accuracy, journals, and math miss it: grip style decides. Tools questioned serve; truths worshipped rule.
items.lessonContent:
Grip style decides model fate entirely.
Provisional holds serve; worship rules.
Limits known keep tools honest.
Idols graduate from unquestioned tools.
Share this: hold one model lightly.

items.title: The Selected World
items.question: News shows fires, not uneventful days; murders, not peaceful millions. Heavy viewers overestimate danger systematically. What does the news map omit?
items.correctExplanation: The uneventful normal majority — newsworthiness filters for rarity, so maps invert frequencies. Viewers inhabit a world of exceptions.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is the uneventful normal majority. Ads, weather, and scores miss it: selection for novelty makes maps lie by omission. Peaceful millions never trend.
items.lessonContent:
Novelty filters invert frequencies reliably.
Exception-maps pose as world-maps daily.
Peaceful majorities never trend anywhere.
Omission lies louder than commission.
Share this: notice one uneventful day.

items.title: The Polled Ghost
items.question: Pre-election models showed comfortable leads that evaporated on voting day — twice in recent memory. What did the polls map instead of the electorate?
items.correctExplanation: Stated intentions of the reachable — respondents who answer differ from electorates who vote. Maps of the willing misread the silent.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is stated intentions of the reachable. Perfection, futures, and counts miss it: nonresponse and shy voters redraw maps after publication. Reachable differs from representative.
items.lessonContent:
Reachable differs from representative sharply.
Silent voters redraw published maps.
Intentions stated wobble before voting.
Willing respondents mislead modelers.
Share this: distrust one comfortable lead.

items.title: The Gaussian Idol
items.question: Before 2008, banks priced mortgage risk with a Gaussian copula assuming stable correlations. When correlations spiked together, what failed?
items.correctExplanation: The worshipped map — copula outputs guided trillions while assuming away the crisis state. Models held lightly hedge; models worshipped detonate.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is the map worshipped as territory. Math, machines, and readers miss it: the formula worked until the unmodeled regime arrived. Idols detonate precisely because altars forbid doubt.
items.lessonContent:
Unmodeled regimes detonate worshipped maps.
Altars forbid the doubt models need.
Trillions followed one formula's idolatry.
Hedge models; never kneel to them.
Share this: doubt one formula's reign.

items.title: The Target Curse
items.question: Goodhart's law: when a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure. Why do targeted metrics rot?
choices: Behavior optimizes the metric, not the goal
items.correctAnswer: Behavior optimizes the metric, not the goal
items.correctExplanation: Behavior optimizes metrics, not goals — effort flows to measured surfaces while purposes drain beneath. Targets redirect work from ends to indicators.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is behavior optimizes the metric, not the goal. Arithmetic, expiry, and retirement miss it: incentives reshape action around what's counted. Measured surfaces shine; purposes rot.
items.lessonContent:
Incentives reshape action around counts.
Surfaces shine while purposes rot beneath.
Targets redirect work from ends.
Metrics rot the moment they're crowned.
Share this: spot one rotted metric.

items.title: The Tested Corruption
items.question: Campbell's law: high-stakes testing corrupts both teaching and the test's own validity. What mechanism rots both?
choices: Teaching to the test plus gaming its edges
items.correctAnswer: Teaching to the test plus gaming its edges
items.correctExplanation: Teaching-to-test plus gaming — stakes redirect instruction to tested slivers while scores inflate past learning. Both education and measurement decay together.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is teaching to the test plus gaming its edges. Diligence, weight, and paint miss it: stakes make scores the curriculum and tricks the pedagogy. Validity dies of its own importance.
items.lessonContent:
Stakes make scores the curriculum.
Tricks become pedagogy under pressure.
Validity dies of its own importance.
Slivers taught; wholes abandoned.
Share this: teach one untested thing.

items.title: The Bred Cobra
items.question: Colonial Delhi paid per dead cobra; enterprising Indians began breeding cobras for the bounty. When the program ended, breeders freed their stock. What lesson slithers here?
items.correctExplanation: Incentives reshape measured behavior — pay per cobra, get cobra farms. Metrics manufacture the phenomena they price.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is incentives reshape the measured behavior. Perfect bounties, economic snakes, and flawless counts miss it: payment created supply. Measured worlds respond to measurement.
items.lessonContent:
Payment creates supply it meant to destroy.
Measured worlds respond to measurement.
Bounties breed what they price.
Effects invert intentions reliably.
Share this: spot one cobra effect.

items.title: The Nail Weights
items.question: A Soviet nail factory rewarded by tonnage produced giant useless nails; rewarded by count, millions of tiny ones. Twice measured, twice absurd. What failed both times?
items.correctExplanation: The metric, twice gamed — weight begat monsters, count begat pins. Every measure grows its own absurdity under pressure.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is the metric, twice gamed. Hammers, alloys, and managers miss it: tonnage and tally each optimized brilliantly past usefulness. Measures fail symmetrically when crowned.
items.lessonContent:
Every measure grows its absurdity.
Weight begat monsters; count begat pins.
Optimization overshoots usefulness reliably.
Crowned metrics fail symmetrically.
Share this: game one metric mentally.

items.title: The Sixteen Boxes
items.question: Millions sort into sixteen types by questionnaire, then treat four letters as essences in hiring and dating. Tests with shaky reliability become destinies. What error is this?
items.correctExplanation: Reifying shaky types — unreliable sorts hardened into identities that hire and fire. Letters describe moods; boxes decide fates.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is reifying shaky types into essences. Reflection, cost, and colors miss it: modest test-retest reliability cannot bear destiny-weight. Sort lightly; never sentence by letters.
items.lessonContent:
Unreliable sorts cannot bear destinies.
Letters describe moods, never essences.
Hiring by horoscope wears lab coats here.
Sort lightly; sentence never.
Share this: unbox one typed friend.

items.title: The Nobody Average
items.question: Quetelet's 'average man' — average height, weight, chest, habits — describes literally nobody: no individual is average on every trait. What fallacy crowns the mean?
items.correctExplanation: Reifying the average person — means describe populations, never persons. Designing for nobody fits everybody poorly.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is reifying the average person. Wrongness, samples, and hatred miss it: averages are real statistics about unreal people. Cockpits built for means fit no pilot.
items.lessonContent:
Means describe populations, never persons.
Nobody lives at every average.
Unreal people wear real statistics.
Design for ranges, never means.
Share this: un-average one design.

items.title: The Ruled Lines
items.question: Straight colonial borders sliced peoples and ecosystems on distant desks; then the lines hardened into destinies, wars, and identities. What did the map impose?
items.correctExplanation: Lines lived as fate — desk-drawn borders became blood-drawn destinies. Maps precede territories they claim to follow.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is lines lived as fate. Cartography, rain, and mail miss it: rulers' pens authored nations' fortunes. Drawn lines harden into lived worlds.
items.lessonContent:
Pens author fortunes from desks afar.
Drawn lines harden into lived worlds.
Maps precede territories they claim.
Borders birth identities they ignore.
Share this: trace one line's victims.

items.title: The Clocked Eternity
items.question: Clock time ticks evenly; lived duration stretches in boredom and vanishes in joy — an hour of queuing outlasts an evening of love. What does the clock miss?
items.correctExplanation: Lived temporal texture — clocks map succession, never savoring. Even ticks measure uneven lives poorly.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is lived temporal texture. Chemistry, ratios, and physics miss it: measurement tracks succession while experience textures duration. Queues eternize; loves evaporate — clocks note neither.
items.lessonContent:
Succession tracked differs from duration lived.
Even ticks measure uneven lives poorly.
Savoring escapes all escapements.
Texture exceeds every timepiece.
Share this: feel one unclocked hour.

items.title: The Unsaid Thing
items.question: Korzybski insisted: whatever you say a thing is, it isn't — words abstract, select, freeze, and leave oceans out. What escapes every label?
choices: The unsaid remainder of the thing
items.correctAnswer: The unsaid remainder of the thing
items.correctExplanation: The unsaid remainder — labels select slivers; things exceed selections infinitely. Saying captures slices, never wholes.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is the unsaid remainder of the thing. Ink, pages, and tongues miss it: abstraction discards by definition. Wholes overflow every word poured over them.
items.lessonContent:
Wholes overflow words poured over them.
Abstraction discards by definition always.
Slices captured differ from wholes kept.
Labels leave oceans outside.
Share this: unsay one thing fully.

items.title: The Priced Lake
items.question: Prices signal scarcity and demand; worth lives elsewhere — a priceless lake sells for picnic fees while addiction trades dearly. What does price map poorly?
items.correctExplanation: True human value — prices track tradability, never worth. Lakes priceless, poisons pricey: signals diverge from goods.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is true human value. Kilograms, wavelengths, and barcodes miss it: markets price exchange, not importance. Dear poisons and cheap lakes prove the divergence.
items.lessonContent:
Tradability differs from importance structurally.
Signals diverge from goods they price.
Lakes priceless, poisons dear: markets map exchange.
Worth exceeds every ticker.
Share this: price one priceless thing.

items.title: The Verbose Code
items.question: Managers rewarding lines of code get sprawling programs; the finest engineers delete code daily. Output metrics miss quality entirely. What rots under counting?
items.correctExplanation: The metric gamed into verbosity — counted lines multiply, elegance dies. Deletion, the highest art, scores zero.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is the metric, gamed into verbosity. Hardware and beverages miss it: rewarding volume punishes concision. Best code is written by erasing.
items.lessonContent:
Volume rewards punish concision directly.
Deletion scores zero yet matters most.
Counted lines multiply; elegance dies.
Erasure is engineering's highest art.
Share this: delete ten lines proudly.

items.title: The Cited Circle
items.question: Hiring by h-index rewards citation cartels, review mills, and salami slicing over discovery. What degrades when citations become currency?
items.correctExplanation: The indicator gamed past meaning — cartels trade citations like currency, mills mint reviews. Discovery uncounted loses funding.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is the indicator, gamed past meaning. Paper, shelves, and speed miss it: currency corrupts what it measures. Science optimized for scores stops optimizing for truth.
items.lessonContent:
Currency corrupts whatever it measures.
Cartels trade citations like coin.
Scores optimized displace truth sought.
Discovery uncounted loses funding.
Share this: read one uncited gem.

items.title: The Lattice Mind
items.question: Munger prescribes a latticework of models — psychology, mathematics, biology — because single models blind their devotees. What cures model monogamy?
items.correctExplanation: Multiple overlapping models — lattices catch what single lenses miss. Monogamy with one model is intellectual celibacy from reality.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is multiple overlapping models. Computers, equations, and experts miss it: breadth of lenses, not power of one. Devotees of single models marry maps.
items.lessonContent:
Lattices catch what lenses miss.
Breadth beats power in modeling.
Monogamy with maps blinds devotees.
Overlap models to triangulate truth.
Share this: wed two models today.

items.title: The Committee Clusters
items.question: DSM categories describe symptom clusters by committee vote, revised with each edition. Unlike broken bones, they name no found essences. What are these labels?
items.correctExplanation: Working maps — descriptive clusters voted into manuals, useful yet revisable. Territories of suffering exceed every edition's cartography.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is working maps, not territories. Essences, photos, and revelations miss it: committees describe, they don't discover. Manuals guide treatment while mistaking nothing for essence.
items.lessonContent:
Committees describe; they never discover.
Clusters guide treatment usefully.
Editions revise what essences wouldn't.
Maps help while territories exceed.
Share this: hold one label lightly.

items.title: The Clinal Truth
items.question: Human genetic variation runs clinal — gradual across geography, with more diversity within Africa than in all the rest combined. What does this imply about discrete races?
items.correctExplanation: They map poorly onto biology — clines know no borders: variation flows gradually, diversity peaks at the origin. Social reality, biological fiction.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is they map poorly onto biology. Prediction, culture, and bloodlines miss it: gradients defy boxes. Races are lived socially, unmapped genetically.
items.lessonContent:
Gradients defy boxes completely.
Clines know no borders ever.
Social reality, biological fiction: both true.
Diversity peaks at human origins.
Share this: unbox one spectrum today.
